blueprint.signature: def annual_pof(beta: float, eta: float, age: float) -> float
blueprint.contract: Returns the chance that an asset of this age fails within the next year, given that it has not failed yet, on a Weibull curve with shape beta and scale eta.
blueprint.idea: The conditional one-year PoF is 1 - exp(H(age) - H(age + 1)), with the cumulative hazard H(a) = (a / eta) ** beta.

lesson.title: 7.3.1 Probability of Failure and Hazard Curves (Weibull)

blueprint.signature: def annual_risk(request: Request, project: Project, year: int) -> float
blueprint.contract: Returns the expected failure cost, in $k, of the project's asset in a calendar year if nothing is done: the consequence of failure times the PoF at the asset's age in that year. The export's age is the asset's age in the plan's first year, so in year y the age is age + y - first year.
blueprint.idea: Risk is PoF times CoF, and the age grows by one each year from the plan's first year.

lesson.title: 7.3.3 Consequence of Failure and Risk = PoF × CoF

blueprint.signature: def risk_reduction(request: Request, project: Project, start: int) -> float
blueprint.contract: Returns the risk removed by a start in a given year: the asset's annual risk summed over every year after the work ends, to the plan's last year.
blueprint.idea: Work removes the risk of the years after it is done; a later start removes fewer years.

lesson.title: 7.3.4 Risk Reduction From an Intervention, Year by Year

blueprint.signature: def coefficients(request: Request) -> dict[tuple[str, int], tuple[int, float]]
blueprint.contract: Returns, for every project and start year the model has a variable for, the pair (NPV of that start, risk reduction of that start).
blueprint.idea: Price each start before the model is built, so each variable gets its own coefficient.

blueprint.contract: Keeps the plan's NPV and its risk removed as two expressions on the Built, and maximizes the one the request's objective names ('npv' or 'risk').
blueprint.idea: Two measures over the same variables are two linear expressions; the objective picks one.

blueprint.signature: def read_plan(built: Built, result: mathopt.SolveResult) -> Plan
blueprint.contract: Also returns the plan's NPV and risk removed, evaluated from the two expressions at the solution.
blueprint.idea: The plan reports both measures whichever one was maximized.

blueprint.contract: Also reads each project's NPV for every start year and its asset (id, age, Weibull shape and scale, consequence of failure), and the request's objective, 'npv' by default; refuses any other objective.
blueprint.idea: The export already carries NPV by start year and asset health; read them where they are.

blueprint.signature: def render(request: Request, plan: Plan) -> str
blueprint.contract: Changes the report in three ways. The funded line's `value $<value>k` is now the plan's objective, what the model maximized (the NPV of the actual starts when the objective is 'npv'). After it comes the line `NPV $<npv>k, risk reduced $<risk>k (maximized: <objective>)`, NPV in whole $k and risk with one decimal, both with thousands commas. Each funded project's line shows `npv` and the NPV of the year the project starts, right-aligned in 6 characters, where it showed `value` and the earliest-start value.
blueprint.idea: A report shows the measure that was not maximized as well as the one that was.
